source.title: I Predict Therefore I Am: Is Next Token Prediction Enough to Learn Human-Interpretable Concepts from Data?
source.authors: Yu-Hang Liu; Dong Gong; Yichao Cai; Er-Dun Gao; Zhen Zhang; Bi-Wei Huang; Ming-Ming Gong; A. van den Hengel; J. Shi

record.file_problem: Whole paper and appendices are present; the text is not garbled or cut off.
record.tranche_reason: The paper evaluates whether SAE features align with supervised concept estimates using Pearson correlation, and measures linear alignment between concept-difference vectors and classifier weights. These are different measurements from Toy Models of Superposition and do not directly test superposition geometry.
record.gate_note: The simulation experiments evaluate concept classification and identifiability, not whether networks with more sparse features than dimensions drop or superpose features. The LLM AsWs measurements concern concept-direction/probe alignment, not superposition or feature dimensionality. The SAE correlations are the results bearing on V4. Literature claims about superposition are cited or discussed, not new results from this study.
record.test_reason: The SAE experiments use SAEs as a tool to promote a new evaluation metric and the authors' structured SAE. They report correlations for SAE variants with no chance baseline (random or untrained features, or random directions). The best-matched feature is chosen by Hungarian assignment among 32,768 features, which can inflate correlations. So the values cannot show whether real models contain SAE-recoverable sparse features beyond chance. The As×Ws analyses test linear concept/probe alignment, not superposition. No result bears on V1–V6 as stated.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that, under their assumptions, next-token-prediction representations approximate a linear transformation of log-posteriors over latent concepts. This unifies forms of the linear representation hypothesis and motivates a probe-based SAE evaluation. In that evaluation their structured (sparse plus low-rank) SAE scores best, though all four SAEs have mean correlations below 0.8.
record.recipe_differences: The paper develops a latent-variable identifiability analysis and evaluates SAE-feature/concept correlations; it does not reproduce Toy Models of Superposition or measure toy-network superposition geometry.
record.method_sensitivity: SAE variant and concept change the reported correlation. The low-rank scaling-factor ablation reports PCC 0.691 ± 0.023 at γ = 10−3, 0.695 ± 0.019 at γ = 10−2, 0.704 ± 0.013 at γ = 10−1, and 0.685 ± 0.021 at γ = 1; these are hyperparameter comparisons for the proposed SAE evaluation.

fits_no_version.finding: Concept-difference vectors align with linear-probe weights (As×Ws near identity) across Pythia, Llama-2/3 and DeepSeek-R1. The alignment holds under cross-validation, against a permuted-label null, and on 8 new pairs.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Final-layer LLM representations encode binary counterfactual concepts linearly, with probe weights aligned to concept-difference directions.

fits_no_version.finding: Best-matched SAE features correlate with supervised concept logits at about 0.5–0.99 per concept, with means below 0.8. Structured and p-annealing SAEs score higher than top-k and batch-top-k.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: On counterfactual-pair benchmarks, SAE variants differ in how well individual features track supervised concept posteriors; none reach full recovery.

record.code_released: not stated; the paper says code and instructions will be openly available once published.
record.peer_reviewed: ICLR 2026 (stated in the paper as published as a conference paper at ICLR 2026)
record.problems: The LLM experiments cannot directly validate the latent variables and instead use 27 counterfactual pairs and supervised probes as proxies. The authors note that constructing ideal counterfactual pairs is challenging, that all four SAE variants have correlations below 0.8 on the compact benchmark, and that some concepts have limited sample sizes. The LLM identifiability analysis is limited to the last layer. Several alignment results are shown only in figures.
record.rows_left_out: Table 3 reports per-concept values for the other three SAE variants on Pythia-70m; these comparator values are omitted to stay within the row cap and because the retained 27 rows preserve every concept result for the structured SAE, while Tables 4–5 retain aggregate variant comparisons for Pythia-1.4b and Pythia-2.8b. Figure-only model/seed-specific As × Ws panels and SAE MSE figure values are not separately recorded; the text provides qualitative summaries but not assignable numerical values for those panels.

untested.parts: No toy models, sparsity transitions or feature geometry.
No measure of feature spread across neurons. SAE-concept correlations lack a chance baseline, so recoverability beyond chance is not shown.
No test of completeness, stability or canonicity of SAE features.

record.verdict_notes: Superposition (Elhage et al.) is only cited in related work. The SAE section evaluates SAE variants and promotes the authors' own SAE. Recovery levels cannot be read as evidence for V4 without a chance baseline: maximum correlation from Hungarian matching over 32,768 features. The reader's V4 supports and limits_scope labels are removed.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not test toy-network superposition, overlap, sparsity-dependent transitions, or regular geometry.
The study does not test whether polysemanticity results from limited capacity or whether important features obtain dedicated dimensions.
The study does not test alternative causes of polysemanticity.

The SAE evaluation measures correlation with supervised estimates for 27 counterfactual concepts on final-layer Pythia activations; it does not test feature spread across neurons or SAE recovery across other model families.
The study does not test whether SAE features are complete, stable, or canonical units.
The study measures concept-difference directions but does not test whether superposed features are one-dimensional rather than multidimensional.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: SAE features trained on final-layer activations of Pythia-70m, Pythia-1.4b, and Pythia-2.8b; tested counterfactual concepts
reader_labels.reason: The reported correlations show SAE features aligning with supervised concept estimates, including high individual concept correlations and structured-SAE mean correlations of 0.752 ± 0.010 and 0.771 ± 0.022; see r01–r35.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: SAE feature recovery on the tested 27-concept benchmark and Pythia checkpoints
reader_labels.reason: Recovery is incomplete and varies by concept and SAE variant; the authors state all four SAE variants have Pearson correlations below 0.8 on the benchmark, while reported averages and individual concepts differ; see r01–r35.
